key_insight: Three joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) formulations trained stably on longitudinal EHRs but consistently underperformed standard masked language modelling (MLM).
clinical_relevance: For patient-record representation learning, these findings favor MLM over the tested JEPA approaches, without establishing clinical benefit.
method: Adapted three JEPA formulations to predict latent representations of EHR sequences.
Compared downstream performance with standard MLM using MIMIC-IV.
Examined how target size and heterogeneity affected prediction error.
evidence_signal: In MIMIC-IV experiments, all three JEPA formulations avoided representational collapse, but reducing target size did not recover downstream performance.
watch_item: Clinically meaningful latent targets remain unresolved, and findings from MIMIC-IV may not generalize to other EHR settings.
paper_title: Are Joint-Embedding Predictive Objectives Effective for Longitudinal EHRs?
